Subject: Concurrency & token snapshot intake — EdgeSpark dedicated sizing

Hi Dana —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. To get our pre-sales capacity estimate over the next week, can you fill out the quick snapshot below (or attach a CSV)? The more concrete numbers you can provide for burst shape and token distributions the faster we can produce a conservative committed-fleet hypothesis.

Quick intake (short answers ok):
- Primary model(s) you plan to serve (name + approximate params / fp/quant):
- Typical user flow(s) that generate inference (API, chat widget, batch enrichment):
- Avg requests per minute (sustained) and anticipated peak QPS (1-min and 1-hr):
- Concurrent active sessions you expect during peak minute and during sustained hours:
- Prompt token distribution (percentiles or buckets, e.g., 50% <= 50 tokens, 30% 51-200, 20% >200):
- Avg response tokens and p95/p99 response tokens:
- Session length (avg prompts per session, typical KV reuse across a session):
- SLA targets (p50/p95/p99 latency targets in ms):
- Any cold-starts or frequent model switches per request? (yes/no + frequency)
- Preferred model footprint (e.g., 13B fp16, 70B q4_0) and tolerance for quantization/latency vs quality tradeoffs:
- Compliance constraints (data residency, retention, KMS/HSM requirements):

I've attached a compact intake template (redwood-dedicated-intake-v1.xlsx) — you can paste numbers directly or drop in a CSV. If it's easier, send a sample of your traffic (edgespark-sample-traffic.csv) and we'll do an initial sketch.

Target turnaround: we aim to return a first-pass fleet hypothesis within 48 hours after receiving the filled sheet. If you prefer, we can book a 30-min follow-up to walk through the numbers live.

Thanks — looking forward to the details.

— Ava
Ava Chen
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood-inference.com | +1 415-555-0187

Hi Ava —

Thanks — attached is a quick export of last week's peak hour and a filled version of your sheet (see edgespark-sample-traffic.csv attached). High level answers below:

- Models: custom instruction-tuned 13B (~13B fp16) for chat + a distilled 6B for light classification. No current plans to serve >70B.
- Flow: user-facing chat widget (40%), async batch enrichment (30%), internal API (30%).
- Avg RPM: 4,200 RPM (70 rps); Peak 1-min QPS seen: 580; Peak sustained hour: ~260 qps.
- Concurrent active sessions (peak minute): ~420 active sessions; sustained hours: ~180 concurrent.
- Prompt tokens: 55% <= 75 tokens, 30% 76-300, 15% >300.
- Avg response tokens: 120 tokens; p95 = 600; p99 = 1,200.
- Session length: avg 6 prompts/session, KV reused across session; some long-running sessions (2-3 mins) with multiple back-and-forths.
- SLA: target p95 latency <= 400ms for chat responses; p99 best-effort but expect occasional spikes to 1.5s during bursts.
- Cold-starts: model warm pool active; model switches only on feature flag rollouts (rare).
- Preferred: prioritize quality for chat model (13B fp16) but open to assisted quantization if we see large cost gains.
- Compliance: US data only; 90-day retention, KMS for keys.

Let me know if you need raw logs; I can share a 1-hour packet with sample requests. Happy to join a call this week.

Cheers,
Dana
Dana Liu
Head of Infrastructure, EdgeSpark
dana@edgespark.ai

Hi Dana — great detail, thanks. A couple of clarifying items from the infra side that change fleet calculus:

1) KV cache reuse — when you say KV reused across session, can you confirm the average % of tokens that are prefix (i.e., repeated system prompts or context) vs new tokens? High prefix reuse materially improves occupancy and reduces per-token cost.

2) Multi-model routing — are chat requests pinned to the 13B model only, or do you expect on-the-fly fallback to the 6B for certain endpoints (we ask because routing and kernel packing affect concurrent occupancy).

3) Burst shape — the CSV shows a 1-min spike to 580 qps. Is that typically a single-minute spike (very spiky) or sustained across 5-15 minutes? If spiky, we often recommend a small, higher-priority burst pool (oversubscribe ratio 1.5x) to keep p95 latency inside the target without overcommitting reserved GPUs.

4) Response token tail — p99 at 1,200 tokens is significant. Are these analytic/batch-style responses that could be routed to a lower-priority pool? If so, we can forecast a tiered fleet with a cheaper quantized path for long tails.

5) Encryption/KMS — confirm HSM/KMS integration required for customer-managed keys or will Redwood-managed KMS suffice for PoC? Enterprise-grade customers often require CMK in their cloud KMS.

If you can reply inline, we'll fold answers into a first-pass fleet hypothesis (GPU SKUs, expected occupancy, recommended reserved count, burst pool size, and latency SLO margin). We can also produce a cost delta for 13B fp16 vs 13B q4_0 to show tradeoffs.

I'll take the CSV and run a quick slotting simulation once we have the above.

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
